query: Which factors best explain negative Yelp experiences?

per_column.name: service_quality_failure
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause of a negative experience (service failures like slowness, disorganization). This is a plausible driver of the outcome and is surfaced from review text, not named in the query.

per_column.name: staff_rudeness_dismissiveness
per_column.rationale: Another candidate cause of negativity (rudeness, dismissiveness). Like the above, it is a driver/explanatory factor rather than a common cause of another treatment.

per_column.name: expectations_versus_reality_gap
per_column.rationale: A further candidate explanatory factor (overhype, not-as-described). Also a driver of the outcome, not a common cause of the other treatments.

judge.rationale: The query 'which factors best explain negative experiences' is served with three plausible candidate causes/treatments extracted from review text (service failures, staff rudeness, expectation gaps). These realise part (a) of the claim: multiple treatments/drivers of the outcome are present. However, part (b) is entirely absent. The system supplied NO confounders -- i.e., variables that plausibly cause BOTH one of these treatments AND the negative label (e.g., restaurant price tier, cuisine type, customer prior expectations, time/wait context, reviewer harshness/rating tendency, establishment type). Without such common causes, any attribution of the outcome to these factors is uncontrolled and potentially biased; the columns form a parallel list of candidate explanations rather than a causal estimation design. The decisive test for surfaced confounders cannot be passed because none exist. Confounder quality is 0.
